title: B&B Direct Bookings Without a Booking Engine
excerpt: How a small B&B can take direct bookings using WhatsApp Business, Google Business Profile, UPI advances and a shared calendar, then win back past guests.
description: Take B&B direct bookings without a booking engine: WhatsApp Business, Google profile links, UPI advances, one calendar and repeat-guest offers.
html:
A small B&B can take direct bookings without a booking engine by combining four simple tools: a WhatsApp Business catalogue with quick replies, a booking or enquiry link on its Google Business Profile, UPI payment links with a clear advance policy, and a shared availability calendar. Repeat-guest offers then bring past guests back directly.

Why a booking engine is not the first step

Many family-run B&Bs in Coorg, Wayanad or the Nilgiris have three to eight rooms. At that size, a full booking engine with a channel manager is often more software than the business needs, and it still needs someone to keep rates and photos updated. Most direct guests in India already reach you the same way: they find you on Google Maps or Instagram, then message or call to ask whether the dates are free and whether the price includes breakfast.

So the real job is not "install software". It is to make that conversation fast, clear and trustworthy, so the guest pays an advance before they go back to an OTA app. A booking engine can come later, when volume justifies it. If you already get enough enquiries, a proper booking flow on your own site is the natural next stage.

Set up WhatsApp Business as your front desk

WhatsApp Business is free and does most of what a small property needs. Set it up on a number you are happy to print on signboards and listings, and that more than one family member can answer.

Business profile

Fill in the address, a short description, hours when you reply, your website or Instagram, and a clear profile photo of the property rather than a logo.

Catalogue

Add each room type as a catalogue item: a few honest photos, the bed configuration, how many guests it fits, whether breakfast is included, and a "starting from" price in ₹. Add separate items for things guests often ask about, such as a plantation walk, a bonfire evening or airport pickup. When someone asks "what rooms do you have", you send the catalogue instead of typing the same reply again.

Quick replies and labels

Quick replies are saved messages you call up with a shortcut. Write them once, carefully, and the whole family sends the same accurate answer. Useful ones:

  • /rates: room types, weekday and weekend tariff, what is included, child and extra-bed policy.
  • /howtoreach: nearest railway station and bus stand, a Google Maps pin, road condition in monsoon.
  • /advance: how much advance confirms the booking, how to pay, and the cancellation terms.
  • /confirmed: booking summary with dates, room, amount paid, balance due, check-in time and host phone number.
  • /houserules: quiet hours, pets, alcohol, visitors and smoking.

Use labels such as "New enquiry", "Advance pending", "Confirmed" and "Past guest" so nothing slips through on a busy weekend.

Point your Google Business Profile at direct enquiries

For many B&Bs, Google Maps is where a direct guest first sees you. Make sure the profile sends people to you, not only to an OTA. Add your phone number and enable messaging or the WhatsApp link where it is offered, and use the website field for a simple page with your rooms and an enquiry button. Lodging profiles can show prices and booking links from partners; you cannot fully control which links appear there, which is one more reason to make calling or messaging you the obvious action. The full checklist for your profile, photos and reviews is in our post on homestay Google Business Profile and Maps visibility.

Take advances with UPI and a written policy

An enquiry is not a booking until money moves. UPI makes this easy for Indian guests, but the policy around it matters more than the payment method.

Payment options

You can share a UPI ID or QR code from your business current account, or create payment links through a payment gateway if you want a receipt and a record for each booking. Use a business account in the property's name, not a personal account, so guests see a name that matches your listing. That small detail removes a lot of hesitation.

Advance and cancellation policy

Write a short policy and send it before you ask for money. Decide how much advance confirms a booking, when the balance is due, what happens if a guest cancels at different points before arrival, and what happens if you have to cancel because of landslides, road closures or other events outside anyone's control. Keep it simple enough to fit in one WhatsApp message.

After payment, send the confirmation quick reply with the amount received. Guests who have been asked to pay a stranger on WhatsApp want that reassurance quickly.

Keep one availability calendar the whole family trusts

Double bookings are the main risk when you sell directly and on OTAs at the same time. You do not need a channel manager to avoid them if you are disciplined about one source of truth.

  • Create a shared Google Calendar (or Google Sheet) with one row or calendar per room.
  • Every booking from any source goes in immediately: guest name, phone, source (direct, Airbnb, Booking.com, MakeMyTrip), amount paid.
  • Block the same dates on every OTA extranet as soon as a direct booking is confirmed. Some platforms support calendar sync through iCal links; where that is available, set it up, but still check it after each booking.
  • Use a hold rule: an enquiry can hold dates for a fixed number of hours without advance, then the dates are released.

Our guide to homestay listing optimisation on Airbnb, Booking.com and MakeMyTrip goes deeper into calendar sync on those platforms.

Make booking direct better, not just cheaper

Owners often ask whether they can simply quote a lower price on WhatsApp than on OTAs. Check your contracts first. In October 2022 the Competition Commission of India fined MakeMyTrip-Goibibo and directed it to drop "wide" price and room parity obligations relative to other OTAs; it treated "narrow" parity covering the property's own website as potentially justifiable. Contracts differ, so read your own OTA agreements before you change rates. The usual way to make booking direct better without undercutting the OTA rate is to add value instead:

  • Breakfast or a home-cooked dinner included for direct guests.
  • Free early check-in or late check-out, subject to availability.
  • Pickup from the bus stand, a guided estate walk, or a welcome drink.
  • Flexible date changes for direct bookings.

Bring past guests back directly

Your cheapest future booking is a guest who already liked staying with you. Many first-time guests arrive through an OTA; after a good stay they are happy to come back directly if you stay in touch.

WhenWhat to sendWhy it works
Day after checkoutThank-you message and a request for a reviewReviews help your listings and Maps profile
Within a weekAsk permission to add them to your broadcast listBroadcasts only reach people who saved your number
Before long weekendsShort note on availability and a returning-guest value-addPast guests plan early for festivals and holidays
Off-seasonMonsoon or weekday stay idea with a returning-guest offerFills rooms when OTA demand is low
AnytimeReferral thank-you, such as a free dinner for the referring guest's next stayWord of mouth stays personal

Keep a simple guest list in a sheet: name, phone, dates stayed, group type (couple, family, friends), and anything they loved.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a website to take direct bookings?

Not on day one. WhatsApp Business, a good Google Business Profile and a clear advance policy are enough to start taking direct bookings. A simple website with room details, photos, location and an enquiry button helps guests trust you and gives Google more to show, so build one once the basics run smoothly.

How much advance should a B&B ask for?

There is no standard amount. Many small properties ask for part of the stay value to confirm and the balance at check-in, while peak dates and long weekends often need a larger share or full payment. Whatever you decide, write it down, send it before asking for money, and apply it the same way to every guest so there are no disputes later.

Can I offer a lower price to direct guests than on OTAs?

It depends on your contracts. The Competition Commission of India's 2022 order against MakeMyTrip-Goibibo addressed wide parity across OTAs and treated narrow parity on the property's own website as potentially justifiable. Read each OTA agreement you have signed. Adding value, such as included meals or flexible changes, is the usual way to make direct booking more attractive without undercutting the OTA rate.

How do I avoid double bookings without a channel manager?

Keep one shared calendar that every family member updates the moment a booking is confirmed, from any source. Block the same dates on each OTA extranet straight away, and use iCal calendar sync where a platform offers it. Check the calendar every morning and after every booking. A fixed hold time for unpaid enquiries also stops dates from being held indefinitely.

Where to start

This week, switch your listed number to WhatsApp Business, build the catalogue and write five quick replies. Then write a one-message advance and cancellation policy, set up UPI on a business account, and create a shared availability calendar. Once these run smoothly, start a past-guest list; if you later want help building a simple direct-booking website, the hospitality page explains what a team like ours works on.
